headline: Anthropic has told investors its revenue rose about 45% to $16.8 billion in the third quarter, just before a stock market listing expected in November.
score_reason: Pool score 9 kept: the first revenue figure ahead of a possible record IPO, reported by several outlets; the company has not confirmed it publicly.
importance_line: People who invest or may buy shares, and the AI companies competing with Anthropic, now have a real revenue number to judge it by, but it is not clear whether it counts gross or net sales and the profit claim is Anthropic's own.
source: Business Insider (also reported by the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg and the Financial Times)
summary: Business Insider reports that Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, told investors it earned $16.8 billion in the third quarter, about 45% more than in the second quarter, and said it made a profit on an adjusted basis. This follows our 14 Oct 2026 item that Anthropic would release new revenue numbers; the new facts are the figure itself and a listing expected in November, though it is unclear whether the revenue is counted before or after cloud partners take their share, and an analyst at PitchBook, a research firm, notes that growth is slowing.
notes: Original WSJ page blocked; text read at Business Insider, which reports it itself ('has learned'), so it is the source. Headline 'nearly $17 billion' follows WSJ; the exact figure is $16.8 billion.
